reason: The tangent and the region bounded by the curve, tangent and x-axis are best understood graphically.

scenes.title: A chord turning into the tangent at P
scenes.purpose: See that the tangent at $P(9, 3)$ is the limit of chords from $P$, and that its gradient $-\frac{1}{3}$ gives the line $x + 3y = 18$.

steps.text: The curve $C$ is $y = 4x^{\frac{1}{2}} - x$. Writing $\sqrt{x}$ as a power first is what earns the B1 for $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 2x^{-\frac{1}{2}} - 1$. The dashed chord joins $P$ to $Q$.
Slide $s$ towards $9$. $Q$ slides towards $P$, and the chord gradient approaches $2\times\frac{1}{3} - 1 = -\frac{1}{3}$, which is the value of the derivative at $x = 9$ (the M1).
The tangent $l$ passes through $(9, 3)$ with gradient $-\frac{1}{3}$, so $y - 3 = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 9)$ (A1ft). Multiplying by $3$ gives $x + 3y = 18$ (A1cao).

guide.what_you_see: The curve $C$: $y=4\sqrt{x}-x$ with the point $P(9, 3)$ on it, a second point $Q$ on $C$ further along, and a dashed chord from $P$ to $Q$. The tangent $l$ at $P$ is also drawn, so you can compare it with the chord.

legend.meaning: The curve $y=4\sqrt{x}-x$ from the question, for $x\geqslant 0$.
The point $P(9, 3)$ on $C$ where $x=9$; the tangent touches the curve here.
A point on $C$ with $x$-coordinate $s$, so $Q=(s,\,4\sqrt{s}-s)$. It moves when you change the slider.
The dashed chord joining $P$ to $Q$. Its gradient is $\dfrac{4\sqrt{s}-s-3}{s-9}$.
The tangent to $C$ at $P$, the line $y=\frac{18-x}{3}$, which is $x+3y=18$, the equation you are asked to show.

interact.do: Start at $s=14$, then drag the slider left in small steps down to $9.05$. You can also drag it right up to $16$ to see the chord tilt the other way.
interact.watch: $Q$ slides along $C$ towards $P$ and the dashed chord swings round to lie along $l$. The chord gradient is about $-0.41$ at $s=14$ and about $-0.33$ at $s=9.05$, close to the tangent gradient $-\frac{1}{3}\approx -0.333$.

question_link.text: The curve $C$ and point $P$ are those of the question. The chord gradient settling at the derivative $2x^{-\frac{1}{2}}-1$ evaluated at $x=9$, which is $-\frac{1}{3}$, is the gradient step (B1, M1). The line $l$ through $(9,3)$ with that gradient gives $y-3=-\frac{1}{3}(x-9)$ (A1ft), which rearranges to $x+3y=18$ (A1cao).

read_off: The live label 'Chord gradient' is the gradient of the line $PQ$ for the current $s$, namely $\frac{4\sqrt{s}-s-3}{s-9}$. As $s$ tends to $9$ it tends to the tangent gradient $-\frac{1}{3}$, which is printed beside it and is the value of $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at $x=9$.

scenes.title: Triangle minus the area under the curve
scenes.purpose: See that $R$ is the triangle under $l$ from $x = 9$ to $18$ with the area under $C$ from $9$ to $16$ removed.

steps.text: $C$ meets the axis where $\sqrt{x}(4 - \sqrt{x}) = 0$, so $x = 16$ and $A$ is $(16, 0)$ (M1, A1). Drag $k$ to $16$ to close the blue region at $A$.

With $\int\left(4x^{\frac{1}{2}} - x\right)\mathrm{d}x = \frac{8}{3}x^{\frac{3}{2}} - \frac{1}{2}x^2$, the blue area from $9$ to $16$ reads $\frac{67}{6} \approx 11.17$ (M1 A1 A1, then M1 for the limits). Going past $16$ would count area below the axis.
On $l$, $y = 0$ gives $x = 18$, so the triangle with corners $(9, 3)$, $(9, 0)$, $(18, 0)$ has area $\frac{27}{2}$ (M1). The green region $R$ is this triangle minus the blue area.
$\frac{27}{2} - \frac{67}{6} = \frac{81}{6} - \frac{67}{6} = \frac{7}{3}$ (A1). Drag $k$ back to see how the blue area changes.

guide.what_you_see: The curve $C$: $y=4\sqrt{x}-x$ and its tangent $l$ at $P$, which meets the $x$-axis at $B$. A blue region under $C$ starts at $x=9$ and ends at the slider value $k$, and the green region $R$ is the area bounded by $C$, $l$ and the $x$-axis to the right of $x=9$.

legend.meaning: The curve $y=4\sqrt{x}-x$ from the question. It meets the $x$-axis at the origin and at $A$.
The tangent to $C$ at $P$, drawn as $y=\frac{18-x}{3}$. It meets the $x$-axis at $B$.
The point $(9, 3)$ on $C$ where $x=9$ and where $l$ touches the curve.
The point $(16, 0)$ where $C$ meets the $x$-axis again, found from $\sqrt{x}(4-\sqrt{x})=0$.
The blue region between $C$ and the $x$-axis from $x=9$ to $x=k$. Its area is $\int_9^k\left(4x^{\frac12}-x\right)\mathrm{d}x$.
The green part of $R$ between $l$ (above) and $C$ (below), from $x=9$ to $x=16$. It appears in steps 3 and 4.
The green part of $R$ between $l$ and the $x$-axis, from $x=16$ to $x=18$. It appears in steps 3 and 4.
The vertical line $x=9$, which is the left-hand boundary of $R$ and the blue region.
The $x$-axis, $y=0$, drawn as a grey line. It is the lower boundary of the triangle and of $R$ beyond $A$.

interact.do: Drag the slider from $10$ up to $16$, and then back down to about $12$.
interact.watch: The right-hand edge of the blue region moves along with $k$ and the reading changes. At the start value $k=12$ it is about $7.35$, and at $k=16$ the region closes at $A$ and the reading is $\frac{67}{6}\approx 11.17$. The slider stops at $16$ because beyond $A$ the curve is below the axis.

question_link.text: The point $A$ is where $C$ meets the $x$-axis at $x=16$ (M1 A1). The blue area at $k=16$ is the integral of $4x^{\frac12}-x$ from $9$ to $16$, which gives $\frac{67}{6}$. The triangle under $l$ from $x=9$ to $B$ at $x=18$ has area $\frac{27}{2}$. Subtracting the blue area from this triangle leaves the green region $R$, which has area $\frac{7}{3}$ (final M1 A1).

read_off: The label 'Area under $C$ from $9$ to $k$' is $\int_9^k\left(4x^{\frac12}-x\right)\mathrm{d}x$, the blue area. At $k=16$ it is $\frac{67}{6}\approx 11.17$, and you take this away from the triangle area $\frac{27}{2}$ to get $\frac{7}{3}$ for $R$.
